title: du
definition: Disk Usage. A command used to estimate and display the exact file space usage of a specific directory and its subdirectories.
simpleExplanation: The 'Which folder is eating all my space?' command. It calculates the exact size of every folder inside a directory.
realWorldExample: You know the hard drive is 99% full, but you don't know why. You navigate to the root directory and type `du -sh *`. It summarizes the size of every folder, revealing that the `/var/logs` folder is inexplicably 500 Gigabytes.

basic: If you run `du` without any flags on the root `/` directory, what happens?
intermediate: What does the `-s` flag do in `du -sh`?

answers.question: What happens?
answers.answer: It will recursively print the exact size of every single file and folder on the entire computer, scrolling thousands of lines across your screen indefinitely.

answers.question: What is -s?
answers.answer: Summarize. Instead of printing the size of every individual file inside a folder, it just prints one single grand total size for the folder itself.

tableData.title: Crucial Command Flags
rows: Summarize. Display only a total for each argument.
Write counts for all files, not just directories.
